outcome: PARTIAL MUTATION -- one record deleted from Qdrant with no re-add. Escalated as a blocker; see esc-3567-2.
notes: exit_code 1 is NOT the expected manual_review-only disclosure here. Two independent causes are present: (a) 40 manual_review records left behind, which alone would make exit 1 expected per resolve_exit_code; and (b) record_error on memory 7d073281-4c5d-4ba3-a01c-3a167f4460f4, which is one of the four per-record outcomes the runbook says a human must adjudicate.

WHAT HAPPENED TO 7d073281: the delete landed and the re-add never ran. MEASURED read-only after the run: POST /collections/fused_dark_factory/points with that id returns 0 points -- the record is GONE from the live store. The traceback shows the failure was raised INSIDE memory_service.delete_memory (memory_service.py:4058 -> _journaled_backend_call:1294 -> sqlite3.OperationalError), i.e. the Qdrant point removal had already succeeded and the exception aborted the repair before any re-add was attempted. repaired=false and no new_id was recorded.

THE ONLY SURVIVING COPY of that record's original 867-char content is the committed dry-run report, docs/toolcall-xml-leak-sweep-2026-08-05/dry-run-report.json at commit a1b77e3265, which also carries the intended 415-char repaired_content. This is exactly the loss the plan's ordering constraint (commit the dry run BEFORE --apply) was designed to survive, and it fired on the first real run.

ROOT CAUSE, measured not guessed: the agent sandbox denies file CREATION in ~/.mem0. A probe from the same environment shows open('~/.mem0/.write-probe','w') raises PermissionError [Errno 13] while the existing history.db still accepts BEGIN IMMEDIATE. SQLite cannot create its rollback journal in that directory and therefore reports 'attempt to write a readonly database'. The file itself is mode 0644, uid 1000, os.access(W_OK)=True -- so this is NOT a filesystem permissions defect on the db.

CONSEQUENCE FOR OPERATORS: --apply must not be run from inside a sandboxed agent session. The Qdrant mutation is a network call to localhost:6333 and succeeds, while mem0's local SQLite history write is blocked -- so the sandbox splits a delete-then-re-add exactly down the middle and produces partial mutations. Re-running the sweep will NOT recover 7d073281; the runbook is explicit that a record in this state must not be re-swept.
